react_native_issues.issue: Non-blocking console warning 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' still emits once during login. Origin is RN Web / Expo Router internals — no user-code offender identified. Unchanged from iterations 105–106.

critical_code_review_comments: TaskFormModal.tsx:338-368 — Confirm <Modal transparent animationType="fade"> nested inside the parent Modal works correctly on react-native-web; testIDs task-form-delete-cancel and task-form-delete-confirm are present and interactive. Good cross-platform pattern (also renders as a native modal on iOS/Android). No changes required.

TaskFormModal.tsx:151-166 — onDelete() → setConfirmingDelete(true); doDelete() closes confirm first (setConfirmingDelete(false)) then awaits api.deleteTask, onSaved, onClose. Order is correct; the underlying edit modal closes only after the DELETE resolves, which prevents a flash of stale UI. Consider handling the failure branch by re-opening the confirm or showing a toast — currently a failed delete leaves the edit modal open with an error string in state.

Delete button (task-form-delete-button) sits below the fold on the ScrollView; playwright's default click enforces viewport bounds and fails. Testing agents should use dispatched click events or scroll the ScrollView (not window). Not a bug — noted for future e2e.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Task DELETE on Expo web preview is fully working now via the custom in-app confirm modal. Preview DB has 0 TESTQA rows. When automating the delete flow via Playwright on the RN-web preview, DO NOT rely on page.click for the delete button — it sits below the viewport inside the RN ScrollView and Playwright's viewport check fails. Use a dispatched click (el.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', ...))) or el.scrollIntoView + JS click. All relevant testIDs: task-form-delete-button, task-form-delete-cancel, task-form-delete-confirm, task-form-modal, task-form-cancel-button, task-form-save-button, task-row-<id>, task-toggle-<id>, task-create-fab.
